explanations.plan: UPI outage containment: payments known-issue IVR, chat deflection, breaks, coaching and overtime
explanations.text: A P1 incident (INC-20261006-6998) opened at 10:31 reports UPI transactions failing with timeout errors because switch-to-NPCI connectivity is degraded. In the 10:30 interval, payments volume jumped to 213 calls against 111.9 forecast (+90%), and service level fell to 4.7% with 59 abandoned calls. upi_payment_failed calls are running at 2.56x normal. payment_status_enquiry is 1.44x and refund_status 1.16x, both consistent with customers chasing failed payments. Staffing is close to plan: agents on phones are near planned, and absences are at or near usual levels, so this is not a supply problem. The marketing calendar is empty. General is also up 30% with SL at 54.5%, likely partly spillover, so it cannot donate agents. The demand is incident-driven, so the first step is to cut it at source. A known-issue IVR message on payments covers the rising UPI failure and payment-status reasons and should stop about 20% of those callers. Chat deflection then moves up to 20% of payment_status_enquiry and refund_status calls to chat at Rs 12 per chat. Moving cross-skilled agents is ruled out because general is at 54.5% SL, below the 70% floor a donor queue must keep. To get capacity quickly, I delay breaks by 45 min on both queues and cancel non-mandatory coaching through the early afternoon. Overtime covers the gap until the outage is fixed, as two consecutive 2-hour offers on payments. The first offers 15 agents (about 6 accept, roughly Rs 4,320); the second offers 10 (about 4 accept, roughly Rs 2,880). That is about Rs 7,200 in total, well inside the Rs 15,000 daily budget and leaving room to add more if the incident drags on. I left callback off for now, to avoid pushing work into the afternoon while the outage duration is unknown.

explanations.plan: Card gateway outage containment for payments
explanations.text: Payments volume nearly doubled at 11:45 (212 calls vs 109 forecast) and service level fell to 2.4%. Card_declined calls are running at 2.67x normal and account for almost all of the excess. This matches the open P1 incident INC-20261009-3059, opened at 11:43: debit card transactions are declining because the card authorisation gateway is failing over to its DR site. General volume is at or below forecast, absences are at normal levels, no marketing campaign is running, and handle times are not materially inflated. The cause is a confirmed card authorisation outage. Cut demand first, then add capacity. The known-issue IVR message should stop about 20% of card_declined callers. Callbacks and chat deflection of payment_status_enquiry take load off the peak. On supply, delaying breaks and cancelling payments coaching are cheap ways to free agents now. A few cross-skilled general agents can move over while keeping general above 70%, though general was only at 78.5% in the last interval, so I kept this small. Two consecutive overtime offers cover the afternoon at about Rs 10k expected cost, within the Rs 15k budget. I put demand levers on until 16:00 to allow for gateway recovery and the backlog clearing.

explanations.plan: UPI outage containment plus payments capacity boost
explanations.text: Payments volume is +69% with service level at 24%, while general's volume is on forecast. The excess is concentrated in upi_payment_failed (2.66x normal, about 84 extra calls in the last hour). This matches open P1 incident INC-20261010-3825 (UPI switch timeouts, opened 14:25), and the jump in volume started in the 14:15 interval. Attendance is normal (2 sick versus 2 usual). The only marketing entry is an unrelated fraud-awareness post from the morning. AHT is not consistently elevated. This is a confirmed UPI outage driving demand. Payments has roughly 40 Erlangs of load against about 26 agents. Demand reduction comes first. A known-issue IVR message targets the UPI failure calls, and chat deflection takes 20% of status and refund enquiries. Free levers come next: cancel non-mandatory payments coaching and delay payments breaks to borrow capacity during the peak. Overtime is then offered in two consecutive blocks. At about 40% acceptance, that is roughly 8 and then 6 extra agents, at about Rs 10,080 if all accepted agents work the full 2 h, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Callback is not used because the outage message already occupies the payments IVR and callbacks would only push work into the evening. Cross-skilled moves from general are avoided because general is running near capacity with unstable service level, and moving agents would likely push it below 70%.

explanations.plan: Login outage containment on general
explanations.text: P2 incident INC-20261024-1535 opened at 11:02: the net banking and mobile app login API is returning 503 errors after a certificate rotation. General volume rose from +47% at 10:45 to +91% at 11:00, and service level fell to 12.8%. login_issue calls are 2.71x normal. balance_enquiry and account_update are each about 1.4x, consistent with customers being locked out of self-service. Payments volume is at forecast (-2.5% today), there is no marketing campaign, and absences are normal (2 vs 1.8 usual), so this is a demand surge caused by the outage, not a staffing problem. First cut avoidable outage calls: a known-issue IVR message for login_issue callers and chat deflection of balance enquiries. Then add capacity to general at once: delay breaks, cancel coaching and a small cross-skilled move from payments, kept small because payments slipped to 77.4% at 11:00 and must stay at or above 70%. Overtime is approved now to cover the period from 11:45 while the incident remains open. Callback limits abandonment during the worst peak. Expected overtime cost is about Rs 5,200 (roughly 7 accepted agents x 2 h x Rs 360), well within the Rs 15,000 budget. Chat deflection and coaching costs are small.

explanations.plan: IMPS outage: deflect status calls, add payments capacity
explanations.text: A P2 incident on the IMPS/NEFT payment hub (opened 12:30) reports outward transfers stuck as pending: accounts are debited but credits are not confirmed, and a reversal job is queued. Payments volume jumped from about +5% to +40–53% over forecast starting at 12:15. All of the excess comes from payment_status_enquiry (1.6x normal, +67 calls) and refund_status (1.66x, +56.6 calls), which are exactly the reasons a stuck-transfer incident would drive. Other payment reasons are at or below normal. Payments staffing is on plan (36 on phones vs 36 planned) and attendance is normal, so this is not a supply problem. Payments AHT rose to 356 s, consistent with harder outage calls. General is near forecast at 84% service level. The KYC SMS and the P4 internal incidents do not match the pattern. Payments is carrying roughly 60 Erlangs of workload against 36 agents. Demand levers come first because they are free or cheap. A known-issue IVR message on the two rising reasons should stop about 20% of those callers, and 20% chat deflection on the same reasons removes more at Rs 12 per chat. On the supply side, coaching is cancelled and pre-14:00 breaks are delayed 45 min to cover the immediate backlog until overtime arrives. Overtime is offered in two consecutive 2-hour blocks, starting 13:15 because of the 30-minute lead time. Expected acceptance is about 8 and 6 agents, roughly Rs 10,000, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Only 3 agents move from general: it runs about 28 Erlangs on 34 agents at 84% service level, so a larger move would push it below the 70% donor floor. Windows run to 16:00–17:15 because the incident's end time is unknown; review once the reversal job completes.

explanations.plan: Card gateway outage containment for payments
explanations.text: Payments volume jumped to 187 calls at 12:45, against 88.5 forecast (+111%), and service level fell to 16% with 48 abandons. The rise is led by card_declined (2.22x normal), with payment_status_enquiry (1.41x) and fraud_report (1.46x) also up. This lines up with open P1 INC-20261001-6607: the card authorisation gateway is declining debit card transactions online and at POS, with response code 91, and is failing over to DR. Demand is outage-driven, so the first step is the known-issue IVR message for the rising reasons. This deflects about 20% of those callers at no cost. Payment-status enquiries can be pushed to chat. Capacity comes from free levers first: delayed breaks, a small cross-skill move from general, and cancelled coaching. Overtime then covers the next hours while the DR failover takes effect. The general move is kept small because general has been running around 78–100% and must stay at or above 70%. Total spend stays well under the Rs 15,000 budget.

explanations.plan: Outage tail: light-touch safety net
explanations.text: The payments surge was caused by the P1 card authorisation gateway incident (INC-20261001-6607, opened 13:00): debit cards were declining with response code 91. In the 15:00-15:45 window, card_declined calls ran at 5.35x normal (264 vs 49 expected) and payment_status_enquiry at 1.58x. General volume and attendance are normal, and no marketing campaign is listed. The incident is now marked resolved and the tail is fading. Payments volume fell from +125% at 14:45 to +24% at 15:45. Staffing is above plan (50 vs 43 agents), and service level has been 100% for the last three intervals. Earlier actions plus the fix have restored service: payments has been at 100% for 45 minutes with surplus agents and falling volume. Further spend is not justified. Overtime, more coaching cancellations and more cross-skill moves would add cost with no service gain. A second break delay would only push the deficit into the evening. The outage message should not be renewed because the incident is resolved, and telling customers about a fault that is fixed would mislead them. As a free safeguard against residual card_declined callbacks and customers retrying, IVR callback on payments for 16:00-17:30 only triggers if waits exceed 120 s. Keep monitoring and escalate if volume rebounds.

explanations.plan: Payments UPI surge containment with capacity protection on both queues
explanations.text: Payments volume is well above forecast (+71% in the 11:00 interval, +46% on the alert), driven mainly by upi_payment_failed calls at 2.2x normal (+103 excess calls), with payment_status_enquiry at 1.38x. Payments AHT is normal, so this is a demand problem, not slowness. Absences are at usual levels (3 vs about 2.8 and 2.5), and no marketing entries exist. The only incident is an unrelated P4 on the HR portal. The UPI pattern looks like an upstream UPI or payment-gateway problem, but no incident confirms it, so the cause is unknown. General has only a small volume rise (+4%), but its service level is falling because it runs about 3 agents below plan and AHT is somewhat elevated. Escalate to IT to check UPI health; if an outage is confirmed, an outage message becomes possible. Neither queue is near 70% service level, so cross-skilled moves are not allowed. Capacity has to come from free and paid levers instead. 1) Delay breaks on both queues across the late-morning peak, which is free capacity borrowed from later. 2) Cancel non-mandatory coaching to put agents back on phones. 3) Use staggered overtime offers on payments to cover the surge, plus a smaller offer on general. With about 40% acceptance, expected overtime cost is about Rs 11,500, within the Rs 15,000 budget. 4) Turn on IVR callback on payments to flatten queue peaks and cut abandons. 5) Deflect up to 20% of payment_status_enquiry calls to chat for about Rs 1,600. No outage message is used because no outage is confirmed.

explanations.plan: General queue surge containment
explanations.text: General queue volume jumped from about normal to +25% at 14:15 and +97% at 14:30, and service level fell to 16.9%. The excess is concentrated in login_issue calls (2.4x normal, about 55 extra calls), so it looks like a customer-facing login problem. Nothing confirms that: the only open incident is a P4 HR portal slowdown with no customer impact. The only marketing send was a newsletter at 09:10 with no call-to-action. Attendance is normal (2 sick on each queue, against about 2.2–2.4 usually). Without a confirmed cause this is an unknown demand surge. Payments looks broadly on plan, though it also dipped to 50% service level at 14:30. Add capacity to general quickly with the free levers first. Delay upcoming breaks and cancel non-mandatory coaching on general. Offer overtime for two hours from when agents can arrive (Rs 360 × about 4 accepting × 2 h ≈ Rs 2,880, well inside budget). Offer callbacks to callers facing waits over 120 s to flatten the peak. Deflect a share of simple balance and offer enquiries to chat (about Rs 12 per chat). I do not move cross-skilled agents from payments: it dropped to 50% service level at 14:30, so it may not stay at or above 70% as a donor. I do not use the outage message because no outage is confirmed. If an incident confirms a login outage, add an outage_message for login_issue and extend the overtime.

explanations.plan: Absorb loan-campaign surge on general
explanations.text: General is running 30-53% above forecast since 09:30 (+46% in the latest alert). SL dipped to 68% at 09:45 and was 83.5% at 10:00. The excess is concentrated in loan_enquiry (2.29x normal, +52 calls) and new_offer_enquiry (3.53x, +36 calls). That matches the pre-approved personal loan email (MKT-2026-551) sent at 09:00 to 900k customers with a 'Call us to activate' call-to-action. Supply looks normal: absences are at or below usual, agents are on phones roughly as planned, and general AHT is near forecast. There are no incidents. Payments is on forecast at about 99% SL. The 10:40 newsletter has no call-to-action and should add little load. About 30 extra calls per 15 minutes at roughly 350 s AHT needs about 11-12 extra agents on general for the next few hours, until the email response decays. The plan stacks levers in order of cost: (1) Move 5 cross-skilled agents from payments, which is free. Payments has 34 agents at 99% SL, so 5 is well under the 30% cap and payments should stay above 70% SL. (2) Delay general breaks in the next hour by 30 minutes, which is free and borrows capacity for the peak. (3) Deflect up to 20% of new_offer_enquiry calls to chat at Rs 12 per chat. (4) Offer overtime to 10 general agents for 10:45-12:45. About 4 should accept, costing roughly Rs 2,900, well within budget. (5) A callback safety net is turned on during the peak so no caller waits more than 120 s without an offer. The outage message is not used because there is no outage. Review at 12:00 and extend overtime only if volume has not decayed.

explanations.plan: Campaign surge recovery for general, 14:00-20:00
explanations.text: General volume is running about 66-74% above forecast since 12:30, and service level has fallen to 3.8%. The excess is concentrated in loan_enquiry (3.5x normal, +110 calls in the last hour) and new_offer_enquiry (4.7x normal, +57 calls). This matches campaign MKT-2026-551, the 09:00 pre-approved personal loan email to 900k customers with a 'Call us to activate' call-to-action. Other causes look unlikely: there are no incidents, absences are at usual levels on both queues, AHT is near forecast and payments volume is normal. General needs roughly 45 or more agents per interval against 29 on phones. That is a sustained gap of about 15 or more for the rest of the day, so capacity must be added, not only reshuffled. Overtime in consecutive offers covers 14:30-20:00. Expected cost is about Rs 9.5k on top of about Rs 2.9k already committed this morning, which stays under the Rs 15k budget. Cancelling coaching frees time on general at once and supports payments. Payments is also dipping (62.6% at 13:45), so this is applied to both queues. Delaying breaks on general for 14:00-15:00 borrows capacity before overtime agents arrive; agents already delayed this morning will be skipped. Callback for long waits on general smooths the peak and cuts abandons. Chat deflection takes 20% of new_offer_enquiry; loan_enquiry is not eligible. No cross-skill move from payments, because its service level is already below the 70% donor floor. No outage message, because there is no outage.

explanations.plan: General queue campaign surge: deflect, protect capacity, add overtime
explanations.text:
General queue volume has been climbing since 12:30, reaching +72% over forecast at 13:30, with service level collapsing to 0%. The excess is concentrated in new_offer_enquiry, running at 5.2x normal (+68 calls in the last hour). This lines up with the 600,000-recipient 'Credit card limit upgrade' SMS sent at 12:30, which asked customers to call. Smaller rises in account_update and login_issue are consistent with the same campaign traffic. There is no customer-facing incident to suggest an outage. Staffing is not the cause: general absences (2 sick) are below the usual 2.3, and agents on phones are only about 2 under plan. AHT is close to forecast. Payments is roughly on forecast, so this is a demand surge on general driven by the campaign. The gap on general is about 15–20 agents' worth of work, so no single lever closes it.

Immediate, low-cost steps on general:
- **Delay breaks** (13:45–15:00), which is free.
- **Cancel non-mandatory coaching** for the afternoon.
- **Offer callbacks** to callers facing waits over 120 s, so the queue is not lost to abandonment and the work returns later when the campaign wave eases.
- **Deflect 20% of new_offer_enquiry calls to chat**, since this is exactly the rising reason and costs only Rs 12 per chat.

Overtime: three consecutive offers on general from 14:15 (allowing for the 30-minute arrival lag) through 20:00. With about 40% acceptance the expected cost is roughly Rs 11,000, inside the Rs 15,000 budget.

Not used:
- No outage message, because there is no outage.
- No cross-skilled move from payments: payments service level has been volatile (44–93%), and pulling agents risks breaching its 70% floor.

explanations.plan: Payments surge recovery: break shift, coaching cancel, staged overtime, digital deflection and callback
explanations.text: Payments demand is well above forecast: 112 calls against 65 expected at 09:15 (+72%). Service level fell to 49% with 14 abandons. The rise is spread across most payment reasons: refund_status x1.53, upi_payment_failed x1.46, payment_status_enquiry x1.39 and other_payments x1.30. Supply-side causes are ruled out. AHT is in line with forecast, so this is not system slowness. Absences are at or below normal, so this is not a sick wave. The only open incident is a P4 internal email delay with no customer impact, so no outage is confirmed. The 08:35 UPI cashback push does not explain the pattern well. The 08:00 interval was already +46% before the push. Refund and status enquiries rose as much as UPI calls. Offer enquiries are actually down. Because no cause is established, this is an unknown demand surge. General queue is roughly on forecast (-4%). At about 300 s AHT, payments is short by roughly 10-13 agents at current volume. The plan uses free levers first, then targeted paid ones. (1) Delay payments breaks in the 09:30-11:00 peak by 30 minutes, which borrows capacity now. (2) Cancel non-mandatory payments coaching until 13:00 to return agents to phones (Rs 150 per session hour). (3) Offer overtime in two consecutive blocks starting 10:00, since agents arrive 30 minutes after approval. Expect about 8 acceptances for 10:00-12:00 and 6 for 12:00-14:00, roughly Rs 10,080, within the Rs 15,000 budget. (4) Deflect up to 20% of refund_status and payment_status_enquiry calls to chat. These are the two largest rising reasons and suit digital handling; estimated cost is about Rs 2,000-2,500. (5) Offer callbacks on payments for waits over 120 s, to protect against abandons while overtime ramps up. No cross-skilled agents are moved from general. It runs at about 21 Erlangs on 24 agents, so moving agents would risk pushing it below 70%. No outage message is used because no outage is confirmed. Reassess at 11:00 and 13:00, and extend overtime only if the surge persists.

explanations.plan: Payments surge containment 14:00-20:00
explanations.text: Payments volume is running about 47% above forecast all day (3021 vs 2057). Service level has collapsed to roughly 20-38% since 12:45, even with more agents than planned and AHT close to forecast, so staffing is not the problem. The excess is concentrated in refund_status (2.05x normal) and payment_status_enquiry (1.74x). There is no customer-facing incident, only a P4 internal email delay. Absences are at normal levels (3 vs 2.6 usual), so this is not a sick wave. The UPI cashback push is a possible driver, but offer-type signals are flat: new_offer_enquiry is 0.88x and upi_payment_failed only 1.36x. The evidence does not establish a cause, so I have labelled this an unknown demand surge. General is close to forecast but slipping, at 37% in the last interval, on AHT. The plan extends deflection, callback and coaching cancellation, which all expired by 14:00, and adds borrowed and paid capacity on payments. Chat deflection targets the two reasons driving most of the excess. IVR callback smooths the peaks. Cancelling coaching and delaying breaks for agents not already delayed recovers phone time. Overtime is limited to the remaining budget: about Rs 10,080 is already committed (about 8 and 6 accepted agents for 2 h each), leaving about Rs 4,900. Two offers of 8 agents each should bring about 3 accepted agents per offer, roughly 13 agent-hours or about Rs 4,600. No cross-skill move is proposed, because general is itself below 70% service level and cannot donate. No outage message is used, because there is no confirmed outage.

explanations.plan: FD campaign surge response with payments staffing top-up
explanations.text: The general queue surge began right after the 11:30 fixed-deposit email to 750,000 customers, which asked them to 'call to book'. On general, volume was +37% at 12:00 and +45% at 12:15. new_offer_enquiry is running at 3.66x normal, and account_update is up 1.44x, possibly following on from the 08:45 KYC SMS. General staffing is close to plan (34 vs 35) and AHT is normal, so this is a demand problem caused by the campaign. Payments is a separate, smaller problem: volume and AHT are on forecast, but it is about 4 agents short (35 vs 39 planned, 4 sick against 2.8 usual), which pulled service level down to 25%. There is no open incident, so this is not an outage. Neither queue can lend agents because both are well below 70% service level, so cross-skilled moves are ruled out. For general, the plan cuts demand and adds capacity. Chat deflection takes FD offer enquiries cheaply. Callback flattens the peak while the email response is freshest. Delayed breaks and cancelled coaching free capacity during the next 1.5–2.5 hours. Two consecutive overtime offers cover the expected tail of the campaign until 17:00. For payments, overtime replaces part of the 4-agent absence gap, and chat deflection takes status and refund enquiries. Expected overtime cost is about Rs 10,000 at roughly 40% acceptance, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Chat cost should be roughly Rs 2,000–3,000.

explanations.plan: Campaign tail cover: cross-skill from payments plus offer-enquiry chat deflection
explanations.text: General volume is running about 47% above forecast. The excess comes almost entirely from two call reasons. new_offer_enquiry is at 6.3x normal (+85 calls in the last hour), which matches the 11:30 FD special-rate email to 750k customers with a 'Call to book' call to action. account_update is at 2.1x normal, consistent with the 08:45 KYC re-verification SMS. Other general reasons are at or below normal. AHT is on or below forecast, so this is not system slowness. The only incident is a resolved overnight batch delay. Absence on general is lower than usual. Payments is close to forecast with 100% service level, despite 5 sick calls. General service level is 100% right now, but that is propped up by about 4 overtime agents above plan, and that overtime ends at 17:00. After 17:00 general loses its overtime cover while still running about 45% over forecast (around 90 calls per 15 min at about 350 s, roughly 35 Erlangs against about 40 planned agents). That leaves service level at risk. Payments is comfortably overstaffed: 100% service level, about 27 Erlangs against 40 agents. Moving 5 cross-skilled agents (about 12% of the donor, well under the 30% cap) is free and should keep payments well above 70%. Extending chat deflection at the 20% cap for new_offer_enquiry and balance_enquiry targets the main campaign driver cheaply: about 60–80 chats, roughly Rs 700–1,000. An IVR callback acts as a free safety net that only triggers if waits exceed 120 s. No new overtime is planned. About Rs 10,000 of the Rs 15,000 budget is already committed, so overtime is held in reserve in case general service level slips after 17:30. Breaks are not delayed again, because many general agents were already delayed today and the gain would be small.

explanations.plan: TV-spot surge recovery for general queue
explanations.text: The general queue started surging right after the 10:50 regional TV spot for the zero-balance savings account (MKT-2026-237, audience 2M, toll-free number on screen). Volume was +53% at 11:15 and +57% at 11:30, and service level fell to 4.8%. The excess is led by new_offer_enquiry (3.71x normal, +53 calls), with spillover into account_update, loan_enquiry and balance_enquiry. AHT is near forecast and staffing is near plan: absences are 3 vs about 2.5 usual. The only open incident is a P4 internal email delay with no customer impact. So this is campaign-driven demand, not an outage or a supply problem. Payments is only slightly over forecast, and its 11:30 service level is 60.3%. General is short by roughly 15-18 agents' worth of work at peak. The plan combines free levers with targeted paid capacity. Breaks and coaching in the next couple of hours are pushed out of the peak. Chat deflection removes up to 20% of new_offer and balance enquiries, the reasons the campaign drives. Callbacks shift peak work to later in the day. A 2-hour overtime offer to 20 agents (about 8 accept, roughly Rs 5,760) covers the core of the spike. A smaller follow-on offer of 10 agents (about 4 accept, roughly Rs 2,880) covers the tail as TV-driven calls decay. Total is about Rs 8,640, well inside the Rs 15,000 budget. No cross-skilled agents are moved from payments, because its service level is already 60.3%, below the 70% donor floor.

explanations.plan: Sustain general cover after campaign levers expire
explanations.text: General volume is running +58% to +82% above forecast every interval. The excess comes almost entirely from new_offer_enquiry: 140 calls against 15.3 expected (9.2x normal), now 34% of the mix against a usual 6%. This matches the 10:50 regional TV spot for the zero-balance savings account (2M audience, toll-free number on screen). Supply is not the problem: absences are normal, AHT is at or below forecast, and the only open incident is a P4 staff-email issue with no customer impact. General service level has been near 100% since 15:15 only because of the overtime and other levers already in place. The last overtime block and the chat deflection have just ended (16:00 and 16:15), while volume is still about 58% above forecast. Payments is stable at about 100% service level with volume close to forecast. The demand surge on general is continuing, but the capacity added earlier is falling away now. The plan restores that cover through to the end of the day. Chat deflection is restarted on the campaign-driven reasons to remove part of the excess calls. A new overtime offer covers 16:45-18:45, plus a smaller one to 20:00. Overtime spent so far is about Rs 8,640 if roughly 40% accepted, and these offers add about Rs 4,300, which stays within the Rs 15,000 budget. Until the overtime agents arrive at 16:45, four cross-skilled payments agents and a short break delay bridge the gap. Payments is well above 70% service level, so it can lend agents safely. Cancelling coaching adds cheap extra capacity. The IVR callback only triggers on waits over 120 seconds, so it is a safety net for peaks.

explanations.plan: Payments campaign surge: absorb the peak and add capacity through mid-afternoon
explanations.text: Payments volume began rising in the 11:00 interval and climbed to 52% above forecast at 11:30 (SL fell to 32%, 27 abandons). The timing follows the 10:55 'Reward points expiring - redeem now' email to 500,000 card holders. The excess is in other_payments (1.77x), refund_status (1.56x) and card_declined (1.33x). AHT is on forecast and payments staffing matches plan, so this is extra demand, not lost capacity. There is no customer-facing incident: the only open one is a P4 on the HR portal. upi_payment_failed is below normal, which also argues against a payments outage. Payments attendance is normal (0 absences logged). General shows only mild extra volume (+9%). Its 11:30 SL dip (19%) came with a one-interval AHT spike (406 s vs 335 s forecast), which looks like noise rather than a new trend. Campaign surges usually peak within a few hours of the send and then decay, so the plan concentrates capacity on payments from 12:00 to about 16:15. Delaying breaks is free and covers the next hour or so. Cancelling payments coaching returns agents to the phones at low cost. Two consecutive overtime offers cover the gap until 16:15: overtime agents arrive 30 minutes after approval, so they start at 12:15. Expected acceptance is about 6 and 4 agents, roughly Rs 7,200 in total, well inside the Rs 15,000 budget. Callback smooths the queue peaks by moving work to quieter periods later in the day. Chat deflection of refund_status and payment_status_enquiry calls (both allowed reasons, and refund_status is rising) removes some calls at Rs 12 per chat. No cross-skilled move from general, because general fell to 19% SL at 11:30 and cannot reliably stay above 70%. General gets a short, free break delay to steady it after the AHT spike. No outage message, because no outage is confirmed.

explanations.plan: Payments evening surge cover 16:15-20:00
explanations.text: Payments is running about 65-80% above forecast every interval. Handling time is on forecast, payments attendance is normal (0 absences) and staffing is above plan, so this is extra demand, not lost capacity. The excess is mostly other_payments (3.8x normal), with refund_status and card_declined also up (about 1.8-1.9x). No customer-facing incident is open; the only one is a P4 HR portal issue with no customer impact. The 10:55 reward-points email to card holders might explain part of other_payments, but it does not explain card_declined or refund_status, so the cause is not established. Service level fell to 73.5% at 16:00, just as the earlier overtime, callback and deflection windows ended. General is near forecast (+10-20%) and at 100% service level. Volume is still running 50-80% high, so the measures that held payments above 80% service level from 15:15 to 15:45 are extended to close.
